resources.string: Run actions with the volume keys

Able's Accessibility service watches volume key presses only while this tool is on and at least one gesture is assigned; otherwise Android does not pass any key to Able. Other keys are never touched. Nothing is stored or sent.

It is the same service used by Screen lock and App lock.

How to turn it off: switch "Button shortcuts" off, or turn off the service in Android Settings › Accessibility › Able.
Recognise the volume key gestures below. Off by default.

Double press: the first press changes the volume as usual; if the second press comes quickly, Able runs the action instead and (optionally) puts the volume back. Single presses are never delayed.

Long press: when assigned, Able holds back that key's press. A short press still changes the volume by one step when you release it, but holding the key to change the volume continuously no longer works for that key.

Both keys together: press volume up and down at the same time and release quickly. Holding both for a few seconds stays Android's Accessibility shortcut and does not run Able's action.

During calls and while the phone rings, keys always work normally.

Only the volume keys can be used. Android does not pass the power key to apps, so it cannot be remapped (Able can only notice the screen turning on or off). With the screen off Android sends volume keys straight to the audio system, so shortcuts work only with the screen on, lock screen included. Actions that change system settings (NFC, Private DNS) need the phone unlocked and may open a settings panel if Able lacks access. Apps that use the volume keys themselves (camera shutter, readers) still receive presses that are not part of a gesture. If Android blocks Accessibility services, shortcuts do not work.
